local_linear_nonintegrability.model: X_i iid Uniform[-1,1], Y_i iid independent Rademacher, target x=0, K(u)=1/2 on [-1,1], h_n=n^(-1/4), fixed fallback only on singular designs.
local_linear_nonintegrability.event: For each n>=2, X1 in [h/4,h/3], X2=X1+delta with 0<delta<h/12, and |Xj|>h for j>=3. Its (X1,delta) density is (1/4)(1-h)^(n-2)>0. Exactly two weights are active and the degree-one design is nonsingular.
local_linear_nonintegrability.calculation: The intercept is (X2 Y1-X1 Y2)/delta. The independent sign patterns (1,-1) and (-1,1), each probability1/4, give plus/minus (X1+X2)/delta. Since X1+X2>=h/2, integrating each signed part over delta includes a positive multiple of integral_0^(h/12) ddelta/delta=infinity. Both expectation parts diverge; this is not merely a large finite variance.
local_linear_nonintegrability.hypotheses: f=1/2, m=0 and sigma^2=1 near0; mu2=1/3 and R=1/2; h->0, nh->infinity and nh^3->infinity all hold. The singular-only fallback is unused on the event.

arbitrary_noncompact_kernel_local_smooth.construction: Let I_j be the interval of width w_j=2^(-5j) centered at 2^j, j>=1. Normalize K0(u)=1_{|u|<=1}+sum_j 2^j(1_{I_j}(u)+1_{-I_j}(u)) by its finite positive integral. Intervals are disjoint; K is finite Borel, symmetric, nonnegative and positive near0.
arbitrary_noncompact_kernel_local_smooth.kernel_moments: Its tail L1 masses are proportional to 2^(-4j), its second-moment terms to 2^(-2j), and its squared-integral terms to 2^(-3j); all sums converge.
arbitrary_noncompact_kernel_local_smooth.design_response: Choose f as a normalized mixture of a constant density on [-1/8,1/8] and |z+1|^(-1/2) on |z+1|<1/16, redefining its value at -1 finitely. Choose a smooth bounded m equal0 near0 and equal1 on the latter interval, and set Y=m(X). Then E Y^2<infinity, f is positive C2 near0, m is C2 there and local variance is0.
arbitrary_noncompact_kernel_local_smooth.failure: At h_j=2^(-j), the positive-u spike I_j maps onto a neighborhood of z=-1. Its population regression numerator contribution is a fixed positive constant times 2^j h_j^(-1/2) sqrt(w_j)=2^(-j)=h_j. No other spike reaches the remote density component for large j; all remaining denominator contributions are bounded, with a positive local constant lower bound. Thus m_h(0) is of order h_j, while the planned local coefficient is0 and would require o(h_j^2). Local smoothness alone is insufficient even with bounded m and finite E Y^2.
arbitrary_noncompact_kernel_local_smooth.location: Retained here as the exact owner scope obstruction; the separate LL counterexample remains a library item.

proved_scope.population_bias: NW quotient Taylor expansion and LL affine-residual cancellation through orderh2. LL proof requires only mu2, not mu4. Compact/local cases preserved; arbitrary noncompact kernels can use explicit sufficient global bounds.
proved_scope.rapid_tail_localization: Bounded K with sup_{|u|>=A}|u|^3K(u)->0 and E Y^2<infinity permits merely local C2 f,m. For integrable v, the far integral h^-1 int_{|z-x|>delta} K((x-z)/h)|v(z)| dz is bounded by epsilon_h h^2 delta^-3 ||v||1=o(h2). Weighted versions control S1,S2 and LL residual tails. This includes Gaussian K with unbounded linear m, without global smoothness/boundedness assumptions.
proved_scope.empirical_bias: NW expectation expansion uses exact centered ratio identity, ER2 and Var(T)=O(h/n), and a binomial good-denominator event. The correction O((nh)^-1)=o(h2) uses the original nh^3 condition. New LL response-law conditional bias uses S1=O_P(h), R0/h2->f mu2 m_double_prime/2 and R1=o_P(h); singular designs vanish in probability. It is not called the classical conditional expectation of a globally integrable estimator.
proved_scope.variance: Truncation proves conditional variance limits for both estimators. LL matrix proof states int u2 K2<infinity explicitly, automatic for compact or bounded rapid-tail K. NW unconditional noise variance follows from L1 moment limits; design-mean variance is o((nh)^-1). Rapid-tail bad-event second moments are bounded by n E Y2 exp(-cnh) via leave-one-out independence and nh3->infinity. Compact/global conditional variance retains only nh->infinity.
